_README: Ground-truth locations of the START/+30SEC button (bottom-right of the 5-button
panel) in the eval frames produced by extract_frames.py.
COORDINATES are in WORK-FRAME pixels (the downscaled frames/ images, long edge
960), NOT source-video pixels. manifest.json carries each frame's scale factor.

status is one of: 'labeled' (center is trustworthy, score against it), 'abstain_expected' (the button is genuinely absent from the image, e.g. cropped off the frame edge -- ANY pick is a wrong-pick), or 'unverifiable' (no trustworthy center could be placed; EXCLUDED from scoring entirely). Do not conflate the last two: 'I cannot label this' is a statement about the labeler, not a claim that a detector should abstain. Conflating them initially mis-scored the homography detector as wrong on a frame where it was accurate to 3px.
localize by eye. These are NOT throwaway frames -- they are the negative test:
the correct detector behaviour is to ABSTAIN, and any confident pick on them
counts as a wrong-pick, not a miss. center on those rows is a rough locator
only and must never be used to score a hit.
PROVENANCE: labeled by Claude by eye from grid/zoom overlays in labeling/.
NOT verified by a human. review_labels.py renders them for spot-checking.
A mislabel here silently corrupts every score downstream, so treat a
surprising eval result as possible label error before believing it.

Frames present in manifest.json but absent here are NOT YET LABELED and are skipped by the eval (not scored as misses). f0400/f0480 are pending: the panel is rotated/small enough that a confident center could not be read off by eye, and a guessed label is worse than no label.

neighbor_xy is the STOP/ECO button center (the bottom row's other button). It lets the eval separate 'landed on the wrong button' -- which would press the wrong thing on a real microwave -- from 'landed near the right button but outside it', which is a precision problem. Both are failures; only the first is a safety one. Frames without neighbor_xy fall back to the stricter radius-only rule.

LABEL ERROR RATE IS THE MAIN RISK IN THIS HARNESS. Seven bad labels found so far across ~29: f0280 (one button left), f0560 (in the gap), f0790 (32px off, blank panel), f0520 (~7px), f0260 (in the gap), f0340 (on the counter), f0580 (in the gap). That is roughly a quarter of first-pass labels. TWO of them were reported as detector failures before being caught -- the detector was closer to the truth than the label. The errors come from reading coordinates off a grid by eye. TOOLS: source_zoom.py to label (4K source, high magnification), then label_check.py to render the label back ONTO the frame, which is what actually catches these. Never trust a first-pass label, and never report a failure without checking the label first.

DE-BIASING (2026-09-21): hand-placed centers were found to carry a SYSTEMATIC offset of about (+2.7, +2.6)px -- consistently up and left of the button's true center, in 16 of 21 frames. The same bias was present in the reference mark, so the eval was scoring a biased reference against biased labels and could not see it; it was spotted by eye on the overlay video. Centers are now refined by fitting a circle to the button on the 4K source where that fit agrees with the hand label to within half a button radius; 'center_handplaced' keeps the original and 'center_source' says which was used.
